<!-- pr-reviewer: c4cab3dcea15e115026ff717f29c2f9fcacbbcb8 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`, so it merges at the next cut).

This is an independent review at the high tier. The PR's own reviewer comment and its label did not count as evidence.

**What looks good**
- `SetModJaw` and `RefitModVise` (`crates/app/src/commands/mod_vise_edit.rs`) each build the new mesh, the marker and the pose moves at construction. They apply them through one `Edit` (`UpdateModel` + marker + `mount::write`), so each is one undo step, and undo puts back the facets, the revision, the marker and the pose together.
- The judged mesh is the mesh you see. Workholding is not in the generation stamp by design (`operation/stamp.rs:256-265`). The post gate reads the fixture's facets and world box live (`fixture::named_boxes_for` / `meshes_for` -> `model::entity_world_aabb` / `world_facets`). So if an op was generated before a jaw edit and posted after it, the post judges the edited steel. I probed `named_boxes_for` around an edit: before z 0..38.1, after z 0..40.0, and after undo z 0..38.1 again.
- Figures are validated when the command is created (`JawParams::check` via `mesh()`), and every refusal names its cause. A side change, a bolt off the grid where the block stands (`fit::footprint_at`), a block hanging off the plate, and a face into the stock are all refused. The `judge_face` change closes the #833 probe: a jaw that was beside the stock before the edit now counts as clear, so pushing it into the stock is refused instead of passing with a warning.
- The refit reuses `fit_pair`, so every refusal of the fit is passed on by name and nothing moves. `partner_of` refuses when the plate has no fixed jaw block, or more than one, and names them.
- The MCP tools `set_mod_jaw` and `refit_mod_vise` run the same commands through `History`. The UI rows only queue `CommandKind`s and go through no world calls (ui -> app). No new file key, so older files load unchanged. The decision record is `docs/decisions/832-mod-vise-edit-refit.md`. No snapshot PNG changed.

**Local results (Windows, trial-merged with origin/main 23c62044, merge clean)**

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| app `mod_vise_edit` | 6 passed |
| app `mcp_mod_vise` | 2 passed |
| app `mcp_plate` | 1 passed |
| app `mod_vise` | 5 passed |
| app `mod_vise_plate` | 6 passed |
| ui `--lib fixture_modvise` (CWD crates/ui) | 6 passed |
| ui `--lib structural` | 4 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I also ran a local probe test, which I deleted afterwards and did not push:
- Refused by name: a NaN jaw height, a negative body height, a slide past travel (26.4 > 25.4), and a body width of 1e300 ("hang ... off the plate").
- A slide edit on the adjustable block undoes exactly (marker, pose and facets).
- A refit against a 600 mm stock is refused: "the adjustable jaw block's place 685.800 mm from C14: it is off the grid".
- A refit against a stock floating 200 mm up is refused: "the stock sits 200.000 mm above the plate, over the jaws".

**Requested before merge**

None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. A huge finite figure (1e300) is refused with a 300-digit number in the message (`seat`'s "hang N mm off the plate"). Capping figures at a sane length in `JawParams::check` would give a readable refusal.
2. The jaw-edit draft (`State::mod_jaw_edit`) is dropped after a successful `SetModJaw` or refit, but not after an undo. After an undo, the draft can still hold the undone figures, and "Set figures" would send them back. The command re-judges them, so this is about UI clarity, not safety.
3. `crates/ui/src/state.rs` is already 4274 lines and grows by 13 lines here (the 400-line law is about growth; noted, not blocking).
4. The dual-station block is held back with good reasoning (`Refs #832` keeps the issue open). Turned pairs (90/270 degrees) and `MountAt::Dowels` are not exercised by their own tests, as the PR body says.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
